subject: Request: support response SLAs & on-call coverage for ACME pilot
messages:
From: Mike Torres <mike.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tina Ramos <tina.ramos@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: SLA & support commitments for ACME pilot

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward with a 3-month pilot. Before we kick off, security and ops need explicit commitments around incident response and uptime. Two asks from our side: 

1) Support response-time SLA: we need a firm P1 response within 1 hour and P2 within 4 hours (business or on-call).
2) 24/7 on-call coverage and a defined escalation path (including an engineer contact who can triage high-severity incidents outside business hours).

Our standard procurement cannot accept vague "best-effort" support language. We understand this may require an exception to your published support terms — please confirm whether Redwood can agree to these response objectives for the pilot and what the process / price uplift would be.

Can you loop in whoever owns on-call and legal? We have a procurement milestone: we need signed terms by March 15 to hit our internal timeline.

Thanks,
Mike

--
Mike Torres
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Health
phone: +1 415-555-0142


From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Mike Torres <mike.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA & support commitments for ACME pilot

Hi Mike — thanks for the clear asks and the timeline. I'm looping in Marissa (our Head of Customer Success) and Priyom (our Solutions lead) to scope what we can commit to for a pilot.

Quick note on expectations: Redwood's standard support for self-serve/hosted customers is 24-hour business-day response for P1s and best-effort nights/weekends for critical incidents. For mid-market pilots we can often offer an elevated SLA via an exception or add-on. I'll coordinate internally and come back with proposed response windows, on-call coverage details, and any required commercial terms (uplift/commitment).

Action: Marissa / Priyom, can you confirm feasibility for a temporary pilot exception (target: P1=1h, P2=4h, 24/7 on-call triage) and whether we need engineering on-call named contacts or just an escalation path to an on-call pager? Also please advise if this requires a formal SLA amendment (legal/finance).

Jordan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA & support commitments for ACME pilot

Jordan / Priyom — following up with proposed approach after talking to SRE and legal: 

Summary proposal (pilot, 3 months):
- P1 response: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour; target remediation communication within 4 hours.
- P2 response: acknowledgement within 4 hours; next-steps within 24 hours.
- On-call coverage: 24/7 support triage via our on-call roster (primary/secondary). For high-severity incidents outside business hours, we commit to paging the on-call engineer.
- Escalation path: support ticket -> on-call engineer -> SRE manager (Sergio) -> Customer Success Director (Marissa) -> Exec escalation (Jordan). We can provide a named on-call contact for the pilot window if Acme requires it, but prefer the paging/escalation model to avoid exposing personal numbers.
- Commercial: to make this binding we need a short SLA amendment and a one-time pilot support fee (suggested uplift: 15% MRR equivalent during pilot) to cover on-call burn and priority routing. Legal will prepare an amendment; finance needs the ACME procurement contact.

Attachments: sla-exception-request.pdf (draft amendment), oncall-rotation.csv (sample rotation view).

Risks / caveats:
- We cannot guarantee uptime-based financial credits for a pilot without capacity reservations; if Acme requires a 99.95% uptime credit, that moves this toward Dedicated/Reserved capacity and additional contractual review.
- Named engineer escalation (direct phone) is possible but limited to SRE manager approval; we should default to pager escalation unless they sign a tighter commitment.

Next steps: Jordan, can you confirm Acme's appetite for the uplift and whether they need named on-call contacts? I will get legal to draft the amendment and deliver a DocuSign link once we have buy-in.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA & support commitments for ACME pilot

Mike — quick update and confirmation of next steps. Thanks for your patience while we vetted options.

What we can commit for the 3-month pilot (subject to SLA amendment sign-off):
- P1: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour, triage/update within 4 hours.
- P2: acknowledgement within 4 hours, next-steps within 24 hours.
- 24/7 on-call triage via Redwood on-call roster; escalation chain documented (on-call -> SRE manager -> Customer Success).

Commercial ask: to make these response commitments binding we will send a short SLA amendment with a one-time pilot support uplift (15% of quoted pilot run-rate). Legal will prepare the DocuSign and we aim to have a signature-ready link by tomorrow.

If Acme requires uptime credits (financial SLA), we should discuss Dedicated capacity — that will be a separate proposal.

Attached are the draft amendment and a sample on-call rotation. Please confirm acceptance of the response windows and uplift and we'll circulate the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415-555-0199
